pins.cuda.pin:
# CUDA toolkit pin (tasks P0.7 and P0.19; bible Toolchain Pins). Shell-sourced by toolchains/cuda.sh.
# The toolkit is assembled in user space under $LASSI_TOOLCHAINS/$PREFIX_NAME from NVIDIA's per-component
# redistributable archives for 12.6.3; no runfile or other installer runs (OQ-010, decision of 2026-09-23).
# 12.6.3 matches the nvcc measured on alpha01 in the P0.6 spike (plans/spikes/p0-nvcc.md).
NAME=cuda
VERSION=12.6.3
# The redist root: the manifest and every archive path below are relative to it.
URL=https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/redist
MANIFEST_URL=https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/redist/redistrib_12.6.3.json
MANIFEST_SHA256=9c598598457a6463eb92889080c16b2b9dc04150e501b8bfc1536d403ba70aaf  # 49142 bytes, Last-Modified 2024-11-20, fetched on alpha01 2026-09-23 (rx 20260923-212205-exec-19f2)
# The components the pinned nvcc and the nvc++ compiles through NVHPC_CUDA_HOME need (plans/spikes/p0-cuda-redist.md):
# nvcc with ptxas, nvlink, fatbinary, cicc, and libdevice; the runtime headers and libraries; CCCL, whose
# nv/target the runtime's cuda_fp16.h includes; and cuobjdump, which the install's sm_80 checks use.
COMPONENTS="cuda_nvcc cuda_cudart cuda_cccl cuda_cuobjdump"
# ARCHIVE_<COMPONENT>="<version> <size in bytes> <sha256> <relative path>", from the manifest's linux-x86_64 entry.
ARCHIVE_CUDA_NVCC="12.6.85 49996208 840deff234d9bef20d6856439c49881cb4f29423b214f9ecd2fa59b7ac323817 cuda_nvcc/linux-x86_64/cuda_nvcc-linux-x86_64-12.6.85-archive.tar.xz"
ARCHIVE_CUDA_CUDART="12.6.77 1126072 f74689258a60fd9c5bdfa7679458527a55e22442691ba678dcfaeffbf4391ef9 cuda_cudart/linux-x86_64/cuda_cudart-linux-x86_64-12.6.77-archive.tar.xz"
ARCHIVE_CUDA_CCCL="12.6.77 934952 9c3145ef01f73e50c0f5fcf923f0899c847f487c529817daa8f8b1a3ecf20925 cuda_cccl/linux-x86_64/cuda_cccl-linux-x86_64-12.6.77-archive.tar.xz"
ARCHIVE_CUDA_CUOBJDUMP="12.6.77 219068 54d0edf14284249baf8e2db1c26c71d079ad7afd1f41779e22f239ff9e8bf60f cuda_cuobjdump/linux-x86_64/cuda_cuobjdump-linux-x86_64-12.6.77-archive.tar.xz"
# Install layout, the one the runfile gave cuda@12.6.3: an archive's bin/ and nvvm/ go to the prefix, its include/
# and lib/ to targets/x86_64-linux/, its LICENSE to licenses/<component>/; include and lib64 are links into
# targets/x86_64-linux, and nvcc.profile finds headers and libraries there.
LAYOUT_PREFIX_DIRS="bin nvvm"
LAYOUT_TARGET_DIR=targets/x86_64-linux
LAYOUT_TARGET_DIRS="include lib"
LAYOUT_LINKS="include:targets/x86_64-linux/include lib64:targets/x86_64-linux/lib"
# Top-level entries left out, by name: cuda_cudart's pkg-config/ holds .pc files whose cudaroot names a system
# CUDA root, which the runfile rewrote to the prefix; no LASSI compile uses pkg-config.
LAYOUT_SKIP="pkg-config"
# Planning bound, in KiB, for the space check before any download: the assembled prefix took 233316 KiB
# (du -sk) in the spike (rx 20260923-212629-exec-290a), rounded up.
INSTALL_KIB=250000
PREFIX_NAME=cuda@12.6.3
EXPECT_VERSION="Cuda compilation tools, release 12.6, V12.6.85"
pins.gcc.pin:
# Host g++ pin (task P4.5; bible Toolchain Pins, Execution Backends native row). The project does not install
# this compiler: it is the build host's g++-12 package, pinned by version and path, so there is no gcc.sh and no
# PREFIX_NAME. lassi.core.runner runs EXECUTABLE --version in the compile sandbox before the first build and
# refuses output without EXPECT_VERSION (Agent Rule 10).
NAME=gcc
# gcc-12 and g++-12 12.3.0 on alpha01: plans/spikes/p4-tt-pins.md, Host build prerequisites (dpkg read in
# rx 20260924-185249-exec-1540).
VERSION=12.3.0
# The versioned driver of that package, outside the scratch disk; /usr/bin/g++ is the host's default, which may move.
EXECUTABLE=/usr/bin/g++-12
# The native row's flags, in order; lassi.toolchains.gcc builds with exactly these.
FLAGS="-O3 -fopenmp"
# The banner text after the program name: /usr/bin/g++-12 --version printed
# "g++-12 (Ubuntu 12.3.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 12.3.0" in rx 20260925-192127-exec-fcd6 (a link to
# x86_64-linux-gnu-g++-12); GCC prints the invoked name first, so the program name is left out.
EXPECT_VERSION="(Ubuntu 12.3.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 12.3.0"
pins.hipcc.pin:
# Host hipcc pin (task P17.6; bible Toolchain Pins, Execution Backends gpu (AMD) row, Host Facts ROCm). The project
# does not install this compiler: it is the build host's ROCm hipcc, pinned by version and path as toolchains/gcc.pin
# pins g++, so there is no hipcc.sh and no PREFIX_NAME. lassi.core.runner runs EXECUTABLE --offload-arch=gfx942
# --version (the class's VERSION_ARGS) in the compile sandbox before the first build and refuses output without
# EXPECT_VERSION (Agent Rule 10).
NAME=hipcc
# HIP 7.12.60610 with its build hash, as hipcc --version printed it in the sandbox on alpha01
# (plans/spikes/p17-frameworks.md, Results 5); Trial.toolchain_pins.hipcc records this value.
VERSION=7.12.60610-2bd1678d3d
# An ELF binary run by its absolute path; it finds its clang, lld, and device libraries relative to itself.
EXECUTABLE=/opt/rocm/core-7.12/bin/hipcc
# What lassi.toolchains.hipcc builds with (HIPCC_FLAGS; a unit test checks they are equal). The target is always
# explicit, in every build and in the --version check, since hipcc given none runs rocm_agent_enumerator to choose one
# (ROCm/llvm-project tag therock-7.12, amd/hipcc/src/hipBin_amd.h:475, :779-792; read from source), so no command
# starts amdgpu-arch, offload-arch, rocm_agent_enumerator, or rocminfo (OQ-002).
FLAGS="--offload-arch=gfx942 -Wall -O3"
# The first line of hipcc --version in the sandbox (rx 20261005-204140-desktop-8r113ei-detached-e805c6d4-54d2,
# Results 5, run without a target); hipcc prints it after a target too (hipBin_amd.h:914-916, read from source), which
# the remote test checks. The second line it printed was
# "AMD clang version 22.0.0git (https://github.com/ROCm/llvm-project.git c849bc16b0e49951d313756f20b73c2b28d321d7+PATCHED:9a6ac45c97a1e511db838c5b46257324d2de1780)".
EXPECT_VERSION="HIP version: 7.12.60610-2bd1678d3d"
# No key names a variable: the measured compile needed only the sandbox's PATH, LANG, LC_ALL, and TMPDIR. The ROCm
# environment script is never sourced, and HIP_PATH and ROCM_PATH stay unset (bible Host Facts).
pins.nvhpc.pin:
# NVIDIA HPC SDK pin (task P0.7; bible Toolchain Pins). Shell-sourced by toolchains/nvhpc.sh.
# The single-CUDA tarball installs in user space under $LASSI_TOOLCHAINS/$PREFIX_NAME.
# 24.11 is the 2024 release whose bundled CUDA (12.6 update 2 and 11.8, per its release notes) is closest
# to the CUDA 12.6.3 in toolchains/cuda.pin; it postdates the LASSI paper, so upstream did not use it.
NAME=nvhpc
VERSION=24.11
URL=https://developer.download.nvidia.com/hpc-sdk/24.11/nvhpc_2024_2411_Linux_x86_64_cuda_12.6.tar.gz
SHA256=39408ac062573936e0d41f34530ab065998ef4b85b6bcccb59287d71135a1920  # first download, 6131381079 bytes, Last-Modified 2026-06-07; clean-tree rx 20260923-045504-desktop-8r113ei-p0-core-8b48
INSTALL_FLAGS="NVHPC_SILENT=true NVHPC_INSTALL_TYPE=single"
PREFIX_NAME=nvhpc@24.11
COMPILER_SUBDIR=Linux_x86_64/24.11/compilers/bin
EXPECT_VERSION="nvc++ 24.11"
# With no GPU driver on the host, nvc++ -gpu=cc80 needs NVHPC_CUDA_HOME set to the pinned CUDA prefix
# ($LASSI_TOOLCHAINS/<CUDA_HOME_FROM>); the bible's compile flags stay unchanged (rx 20260923-045559-desktop-8r113ei-p0-core-778e).
CUDA_HOME_FROM=cuda@12.6.3
pins.polygeist.pin:
# Polygeist pin (task P5.5; bible Toolchain Pins, MLIR stacks; plans/spikes/p5-mlir-pins.md, Results 1, 4, and 5).
# Shell-sourced by toolchains/polygeist.sh, which builds in place at $LASSI_TOOLCHAINS/$PREFIX_NAME: LLVM with clang
# and MLIR, and Polygeist as LLVM's external project, in one in-tree build (README.md:89-95), of TARGETS only, with no
# install (the space plan of OQ-049). The tree is an install once it holds lassi-install.txt. The script's space check
# plans for both MLIR stacks together whichever is built first (INSTALL_KIB, RESERVE_KIB). Values read from upstream
# with `gh api` on 2026-10-13 and checked again on 2026-10-26; file:line citations are at COMMIT for Polygeist and at
# LLVM_COMMIT for llvm-project.
NAME=polygeist
# llvm/Polygeist main's head (2024-07-31), the commit the P5 plan's rule chose (bible Toolchain Pins, MLIR stacks).
# Polygeist has no release, so VERSION is the commit's first eight characters, as tt-metal.pin's is; PREFIX_NAME is
# <NAME>@<VERSION> (lassi/toolchains/pins.py). README.md:10 clones https://github.com/llvm/Polygeist.
VERSION=77c04bb2
PREFIX_NAME=polygeist@77c04bb2
COMMIT=77c04bb2a7a2406ca9480bcc9e729b07d2c8d077
URL=https://github.com/llvm/Polygeist.git
# LLVM is the llvm-project gitlink in COMMIT's tree, at the path and from the URL .gitmodules:1-3 names. The script
# fetches it by commit at depth 1, never through `git submodule` (its whole history), and checks that Polygeist's tree
# records LLVM_COMMIT at LLVM_SUBMODULE. This is the CPU stack's own LLVM: Polygeist does not build against tt-mlir's
# LLVM (spike, Results 1), so the two stacks never share one.
LLVM_COMMIT=26eb4285b56edd8c897642078d91f16ff0fd3472
LLVM_URL=https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project.git
LLVM_SUBMODULE=llvm-project
# What Trial.toolchain_pins.llvm records for this stack: LLVM's PACKAGE_VERSION, 18.0.0git (llvm/CMakeLists.txt:11-26),
# and LLVM_COMMIT's first eight characters, so this LLVM is never mistaken for tt-mlir's (22.0.0git at 4efe170d, which
# only the tt_mlir field names, through tt-mlir.pin's VERSION). Today the runner records each pin's VERSION alone
# (lassi/core/runner.py, _pin_versions), so polygeist gets VERSION and nothing fills llvm yet; recording LLVM_VERSION
# in the llvm field comes in a later task (P5.6 or P5.7), with a Decision Log entry.
LLVM_VERSION=18.0.0git-26eb4285
# The in-tree build of README.md:89-95: LLVM's llvm/ directory, projects clang and mlir (:90; no polly, which only
# Polymer with ISL needs, README.md:37), Polygeist as the external project polygeist (:91; llvm/tools/CMakeLists.txt:54-57
# adds it, and llvm/cmake/modules/AddLLVM.cmake:1491-1493 caches its source directory, which the script sets, as :92
# does), the host target (:93; llvm/cmake/config-ix.cmake:520-528 turns it into X86 in a variable, while the cache
# keeps "host"; LLVM's default is all, llvm/CMakeLists.txt:469-470, and cgeist links ${LLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD},
# tools/cgeist/CMakeLists.txt:2; the NVPTX and AMDGPU code of lib/polygeist/Passes/SerializeToCubin.cpp:18 and
# SerializeToHsaco.cpp:4 compiles only with CUDA or ROCm on), and assertions on (:94; tt-mlir.pin builds its LLVM so
# too). Four changes:
# - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE is Release, the P5 plan's planning decision (plans/p5-ir.md, "One LLVM or two"), where
#   README.md:95 has DEBUG; upstream CI builds this LLVM as Release (.github/workflows/build.yml:18, :91). Assertions
#   stay on as set, since LLVM turns them off by default outside Debug (llvm/CMakeLists.txt:589-593).
# - LLVM_INCLUDE_TESTS is off, by the same planning decision; LLVM's default is on (llvm/CMakeLists.txt:737), and
#   MLIR's and clang's tests follow it (mlir/CMakeLists.txt:126-128, clang/CMakeLists.txt:438-440), so mlir-opt links
#   no MLIR test library (mlir/tools/mlir-opt/CMakeLists.txt:14). Polygeist's own lit targets are still configured
#   and name FileCheck, not, count, split-file, llvm-config, cgeist, clang, and polygeist-opt as dependencies
#   (test/CMakeLists.txt:8
pins.tt-metal.pin:
# tt-metal pin (task P4.2; bible Toolchain Pins, joint pin; plans/spikes/p4-tt-pins.md). Shell-sourced by
# toolchains/tt-metal.sh, which fetches COMMIT and its submodules by sha at depth 1 and builds the tree in place
# at $LASSI_TOOLCHAINS/$PREFIX_NAME, an install once it holds lassi-install.txt. The runtime finds the tree
# through TT_METAL_RUNTIME_ROOT (tt_metal/llrt/rtoptions.cpp; otherwise /usr/libexec/tt-metalium).
# lassi.toolchains.ttmetal_build also reads it: EXECUTABLE, EXPECT_VERSION, and the HOST_* build line (P4.10).
# Task P17.42 (the owner, 2026-10-26: "Tracy should definitely get done"; the answer to OQ-105 of
# plans/spikes/tt-perf.md, option (b): the main pin built with Tracy) builds the same commit with ENABLE_TRACY=ON, the
# only build in which tt-metal compiles its device profiler (tt_metal/llrt/rtoptions.cpp:673-681), with the Tracy
# client built to send no UDP broadcast and to listen on the loopback interface only. It installs under a new
# PREFIX_NAME, so the P4.2 install at tt-metal@5280a9cf stays on alpha01, neither replaced nor removed. A pin change is a
# Decision Log entry (Agent Rule 10).
NAME=tt-metal
# The TT_METAL_VERSION of tt-mlir 0.9.0.dev20260221's third_party/CMakeLists.txt (2026-02-17).
COMMIT=5280a9cfb00998fd49667a29523d03aee905c129
# VERSION names the source; BUILD the build variant (lassi/toolchains/pins.py): a trial records <VERSION>-<BUILD>
# (recorded_version), and PREFIX_NAME is <NAME>@<VERSION>-<BUILD>. The script checks COMMIT. Packs, prompts, and indexes
# built from the tree's sources keep VERSION, since the sources are the same.
VERSION=5280a9cf
BUILD=tracy
PREFIX_NAME=tt-metal@5280a9cf-tracy
URL=https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal.git
# The gitlinks at COMMIT, <path>:<commit>, exactly; none nests submodules.
SUBMODULES="tt_metal/third_party/tt_llk:f990966829c2831bf2a58d8ce31779acbb476139 tt_metal/third_party/umd:0450f1be3a21cbf17adb97517038586a6a3af4c0 tt_metal/third_party/tracy:0aaefbb689b4c60694edc905545fc4709fd13f6a models/demos/t3000/llama2_70b/reference/llama:29125b7ad8b5513eeaa4417ed92892bf39c8bd74"
# Configure downloads, each checked by tt-metal's CMake: sfpi (tt_metal/sfpi-version, FetchContent URL_HASH)
# into runtime/sfpi, and CPM.cmake (EXPECTED_HASH). CPM packages are recorded in lassi-cpm-sources.txt.
SFPI_VERSION=7.25.0
SFPI_FILENAME=sfpi_7.25.0_x86_64_debian.txz
SFPI_URL=https://github.com/tenstorrent/sfpi/releases/download/7.25.0/sfpi_7.25.0_x86_64_debian.txz
SFPI_SHA256=6a8883c448df537d9661e239e67721b1ba2a4d0e8ea7a573070d2f6c6d015093  # 88805716 bytes
CPM_URL=https://github.com/cpm-cmake/CPM.cmake/releases/download/v0.40.2/CPM.cmake
CPM_SHA256=c8cdc32c03816538ce22781ed72964dc864b2a34a310d3b7104812a5ca2d835d  # 41017 bytes
# The configuration of the pin's ttsim CI build, but for what is built (owner, 2026-09-25: least CPU on
# alpha01): bindings, tests, and ccache off. tt-metal.sh says why the example binaries keep CI's flags. Since task
# P17.42, also but for Tracy: CI's --disable-profiler (ENABLE_TRACY=OFF) becomes ENABLE_TRACY=ON, tt-metal's own
# default (cmake/project_options.cmake:7), which cmake/tracy.cmake:6-10 passes to the Tracy client as TRACY_ENABLE
# before its add_subdirectory (:20). TRACY_NO_BROADCAST=ON and TRACY_ONLY_LOCALHOST=ON are the client's options at
# tracy 0aaefbb6 (CMakeLists.txt:71 and :70): its set_option macro (:55-63) runs option() and, when the option is on,
# adds it as a PUBLIC compile definition of TracyClient, and a -D on this configure line makes the cache entry before
# option() runs, which keeps it. With TRACY_NO_BROADCAST the client never opens its UDP broadcast
# (public/client/TracyProfiler.cpp:1743-1764); with TRACY_ONLY_LOCALHOST its listener asks getaddrinfo without
# AI_PASSIVE, so it binds the loopback address, IPv4 only (public/common/TracySocket.cpp:457-461, :478). A sandboxed
# run has its own empty network namespace anyway (lassi.executors.sandbox, unshare -rinmpfu). tracy.cmake's
# tracy_tools target (:
pins.tt-mlir-runtime.pin:
# tt-mlir runtime pin (task P17.48; the owner's answer to OQ-111 of 2026-10-29, option (b): a tt-mlir runtime at the
# joint pin with MLIR's Python bindings and ttrt, in a new prefix; plans/spikes/ttir-d2m.md, section 4;
# plans/spikes/ttmlir-runtime.md). Shell-sourced by toolchains/tt-mlir-runtime.sh, which builds in place at
# $LASSI_TOOLCHAINS/$PREFIX_NAME: flatbuffers into TOOLCHAIN_DIR, a venv with a wheelhouse, LLVM with tt-mlir's
# patch and MLIR's Python bindings, and tt-mlir with its runtime, which fetches and builds tt-mlir's own tt-metal. The
# compiler install at $LASSI_TOOLCHAINS/$COMPILER_PREFIX_NAME (toolchains/tt-mlir.pin) is never written to, read as a
# build input, or moved; the script refuses a layout in which either prefix holds the other. Same sources as
# toolchains/tt-mlir.pin (the values below repeat it, and the tests hold them equal): another build of them, so a
# trial records <VERSION>-<BUILD> (lassi/toolchains/pins.py, recorded_version). Values read from upstream on
# 2026-10-29; file:line citations are at COMMIT unless they name another tree. A pin change is a Decision Log entry.
NAME=tt-mlir
VERSION=0.9.0.dev20260221
BUILD=runtime
PREFIX_NAME=tt-mlir@0.9.0.dev20260221-runtime
COMPILER_PREFIX_NAME=tt-mlir@0.9.0.dev20260221
COMMIT=5f396fd6ef85780bf1b6b85bef9c7d2f84a85f3c
URL=https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir.git
# cmake/modules/TTMLIRVersion.cmake:44-63 describes the newest v<major>.<minor> tag and counts the commits since it;
# ttrt's wheel takes that version (tools/ttrt/CMakeLists.txt:22-24, setup.py:11-15), PROJECTED 0.0.2995 (the
# compare API's count, toolchains/tt-mlir.pin:15-18); the script reads the count from its clone.
VERSION_TAG=v0.0
VERSION_TAG_COMMIT=a637748e5521f78546027114fabf2023be63901a
# LLVM and flatbuffers at the commits env/CMakeLists.txt pins (:4-5), fetched by commit at depth 1 into this prefix,
# as toolchains/tt-mlir.sh fetches them; the compiler install's trees are not reused.
LLVM_COMMIT=4efe170d858eb54432f520abb4e7f0086236748b
LLVM_URL=https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project.git
FLATBUFFERS_COMMIT=fb9afbafc7dfe226b9db54d4923bfb8839635274
FLATBUFFERS_URL=https://github.com/google/flatbuffers.git
LLVM_PATCH=env/patches/affine-allow-symbol-vars.patch
LLVM_PATCH_BLOB=2ffdae14d2bcb8244189d8eb044dd093642fa436
LLVM_PATCH_SHA256=61e8ae545e956551b87dc7fb63067d570035becbcf0636ce81ca0971e30f3aac
# The venv's packages, each pinned by version and sha256, a superset of the compiler venv's at the same versions; the
# file's header says why each is there. torch comes from PYTHON_EXTRA_INDEX (tools/ttrt/requirements.txt:1). They are
# downloaded into WHEELHOUSE_DIR and installed from it; ttrt's build later runs pip there offline (PIP_FIND_LINKS).
PYTHON_REQUIREMENTS=tt-mlir-runtime-requirements.txt
PYTHON_EXTRA_INDEX=https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
WHEELHOUSE_DIR=toolchain/wheelhouse
# The pip and setuptools that Ubuntu's python3.10 -m venv seeds (rx 20261029-175313-exec-9dd3 read pip 22.0.2 and
# setuptools 59.6.0 in the compiler's venv); the requirements change neither. ttrt's `pip wheel .`
# (tools/ttrt/CMakeLists.txt:27) takes the legacy `setup.py bdist_wheel` path at this pip (src/pip/_internal/
# pyproject.py:93-94 and wheel_builder.py:63-65 at pip 22.0.2), which runs this setuptools with the requirements'
# wheel package and needs no build environment from an index.
PIP_EXPECT="pip 22.0.2"
SETUPTOOLS_EXPECT=59.6.0
# flatbuffers as toolchains/tt-mlir.pin builds it (env/CMakeLists.txt:33-40).
FLATBUFFERS_CMAKE_FLAGS="-G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DFLATBUFFERS_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON"
# LLVM as env/CMakeLists.txt:56-71 configures it, with two changes, both toolchains/tt-mlir.pin's: Release (upstream
# MinSizeRel, :8) and LLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD host (tt-mlir links the host's X86 libraries alone,
# lib/Target/LLVM/CMakeLists.txt:11-16). Unlike the compiler pin, MLIR's Python bindings are on, as upstream sets
# them (:68): tools/CMakeLists.txt:
pins.tt-mlir.pin:
# tt-mlir pin (task P5.4; bible Toolchain Pins, joint pin and MLIR stacks; plans/spikes/p5-mlir-pins.md, Results 2,
# 4, and 5). Shell-sourced by toolchains/tt-mlir.sh, which builds in place at $LASSI_TOOLCHAINS/$PREFIX_NAME:
# flatbuffers into TOOLCHAIN_DIR, the venv, LLVM with tt-mlir's patch, and tt-mlir's TARGETS against LLVM's build
# tree, with no LLVM install (the space plan of OQ-049). The tree is an install once it holds lassi-install.txt.
# The script never runs tt-mlir's env/CMakeLists.txt, which would make a Python 3.12 venv with torch and run
# tt-metal's debugger installer (spike, Results 2), or env/activate, whose variables it sets itself. Values read
# from upstream with `gh api` on 2026-10-12; file:line citations are at COMMIT unless they name another commit.
NAME=tt-mlir
# The joint pin's release, tag 0.9.0.dev20260221, whose commit is COMMIT. PREFIX_NAME is <NAME>@<VERSION>
# (lassi/toolchains/pins.py); the script checks COMMIT.
VERSION=0.9.0.dev20260221
PREFIX_NAME=tt-mlir@0.9.0.dev20260221
COMMIT=5f396fd6ef85780bf1b6b85bef9c7d2f84a85f3c
URL=https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir.git
# cmake/modules/TTMLIRVersion.cmake lists the local tags matching v[0-9]*.[0-9]* (:10-15), fetches every tag from an
# "upstream" remote when there is none (:17-40), and describes the newest (:44-49), which :60 needs. tt-mlir's only
# such tag is v0.0, a lightweight tag on VERSION_TAG_COMMIT, 2995 commits before COMMIT (the matching-refs and
# compare APIs). The script fetches COMMIT with its history and this tag alone, so the configure fetches no tags.
VERSION_TAG=v0.0
VERSION_TAG_COMMIT=a637748e5521f78546027114fabf2023be63901a
# LLVM and flatbuffers at the commits env/CMakeLists.txt pins (:4-5) from the repositories it names (:41, :72). The
# script fetches each by commit at depth 1 (upstream clones them whole; the files are the same).
LLVM_COMMIT=4efe170d858eb54432f520abb4e7f0086236748b
LLVM_URL=https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project.git
FLATBUFFERS_COMMIT=fb9afbafc7dfe226b9db54d4923bfb8839635274
FLATBUFFERS_URL=https://github.com/google/flatbuffers.git
# The patch env/CMakeLists.txt:55 applies to LLVM, read from the tt-mlir tree and checked before it is applied: its

# LLVM as env/CMakeLists.txt:56-71 configures it, with four changes. CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE is Release, the P5 plan's

# or bindings); upstream's default is MinSizeRel (:8), and the spike's space projection allows for Release (Results
# 5). The MLIR Python bindings are off (:68 has them on): tt-mlir's are off too, and upstream installs their Python
# requirements before LLVM's configure (:55), which the script does not. LLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD is host, as tt-mlir
# main builds it since its pull request 7130 (tt-mlir links the host's X86 libraries alone,
